partner_json_extract.hero: Uber × Navier — the water layer of the world's mobility platform
partner_json_extract.why_now: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water — roughly ten times more efficient than a conventional hull, faster, smoother, and quiet — and it needs no new infrastructure: it uses the oceans and berths that already exist, unlike flying taxis that need vertiports and fresh certification. The model is already real and ramping: a ~100-vessel network is being deployed in the Maldives ($100M, three-year phasing). Uber has shown it will put partner-operated autonomous fleets in its app; this is the same model on the water.
partner_json_extract.network_thesis: One app. Every coastline. A water surface nobody else has claimed. | Sixty-five marinas in a single metro region imply over two thousand point-to-point routes — a dense demand graph hiding in plain sight on the water. Uber already owns that demand in its coastal markets; Navier supplies a uniform, software-defined, autonomy-ready fleet that books door-to-door beside UberX at every pier. Start with one market or commit to the network — the supply standard is identical everywhere.
partner_json_extract.multimodal_fit: Same playbook as Uber's robotaxi partnerships: partner-operated supply, Uber-owned demand and rider experience. Every water leg books door-to-door with an UberX at each pier — one app, one account, a new surface.
partner_json_extract.differentiation: {'why_navier': 'Software-defined and autonomy-ready, a Turkey factory for supply, and at-scale proof in the Maldives — one uniform fleet Uber can deploy in any coastal market.'}
partner_json_extract.the_ask: {'navier_brings': 'The software-defined foiling fleet, fleet operations, and a uniform integration spec deployable in any market.', 'partner_brings': 'Demand, the app and rider relationship, and a first market to prove the in-app water tier.', 'next_step': 'Pick a launch market — the Gulf, Miami, or the Bay are ready now — and scope a Phase-1 in-app foiling tier.'}
partner_json_extract.close: Every coastline, one app. | Uber's demand, Navier's supply — the global water-mobility network, market by market.
